def: A policy that refuses everything unless a rule allows it, so a forgotten case fails closed instead of open.
The proxy that is the sandbox's only route out, parsing each URL and checking it against an allowlist and a ledger.
A count of requests and bytes per day kept at the gate, outside the sandbox, with hard caps.
A way to move information using a mechanism not designed for communication, such as the choice of which allowed URL to fetch.
The limit L at most N times log2 M on the bits that can leave through N requests with M distinguishable forms.
A Linux kernel feature that caps the CPU, memory, processes and disk input and output of a set of processes.
A limit on elapsed time held by the parent process, which stops an idle process that uses no CPU time.
A shared host that accepts content from strangers, so allowing it lets an agent read or write data anyone can reach.
A copy of the packages and files a run needs, fetched before the run so the sandbox needs no network at run time.
The signal sent to a process that exceeds its CPU-time limit; its number is 24 on macOS and Linux.
